title: Composite and inverse functions
summary: A [[composite-function|composite function]] feeds one [[function|function]]'s output into another: $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$. In a model it chains quantities, such as time to items to cost. An [[inverse-function|inverse function]] undoes $f$, and a parabola gets one once you keep only one side of its vertex.

goals.text: Form and evaluate $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$, applying the functions in the right order.
Build a [[composite-function|composite function]] from two models, interpret it in context, and solve equations it gives with your GDC.
Use $(f \circ f^{-1})(x) = (f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = x$, and find $f^{-1}(x)$ and its [[domain|domain]].
Restrict the domain of a quadratic so it has an inverse, choose the right sign of the square root, and interpret $f^{-1}(a)$ in context.

synonyms: how to find an inverse function
restricting the domain for an inverse
f inverse of f of x equals x

before.prompt: A stone's height is $h(t) = 50 - 4.9t^{2}$ metres after $t$ seconds. Find $h(2)$.
before.explain: $h(2) = 50 - 4.9 \times 4 = 30.4$ m. $40.2$ forgets to square, and $-46.04$ squares $4.9 \times 2$. Revise it in {{lesson:2.2}}.

before.prompt: A function $f$ has domain $0 \le x \le 5$ and [[range|range]] $2 \le f(x) \le 17$, and it has an inverse. What is the domain of $f^{-1}$?
before.hint: The inverse swaps inputs and outputs.
before.explain: $f^{-1}$ takes the outputs of $f$ as its inputs, so its domain is the range of $f$: $2 \le x \le 17$. Revise it in {{lesson:2.2}}.

blocks.text: Think of each function as a machine. Put $x$ into $g$, then put its output, $g(x)$, into $f$. The two machines together make one new function: a [[composite-function|composite function]].

blocks.statement: The composite function $f \circ g$ is defined by $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$. It applies $g$ first, then applies $f$ to the result.
blocks.plain: Do $g$, then do $f$ to whatever $g$ gave you.

blocks.text: Read $f \circ g$ as “$f$ of $g$”. The function written next to $x$ acts first. So in $f \circ g$, $g$ acts first even though $f$ is written first.

blocks.question: Let $f(x) = 2x + 5$ and $g(x) = x^{2} - 3$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Find $(f \circ g)(4)$ and $(g \circ f)(4)$.
steps: $(f \circ g)(4) = f(g(4))$, so start with the inside function: $g(4) = 4^{2} - 3 = 13$.
Put this output into $f$: $f(13) = 2(13) + 5 = 31$.
For the other order, start with $f$: $f(4) = 2(4) + 5 = 13$.
Then $g(13) = 13^{2} - 3 = 166$. So $(g \circ f)(4) = 166$: a different number, so the order matters.

blocks.prompt: Let $f(x) = x + 4$ and $g(x) = 3x^{2}$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Find $(g \circ f)(x)$.
blocks.hint: Which function acts on $x$ first? Put its output into the other one.
blocks.explain: $f$ acts first, giving $x + 4$. Then $g$ squares it and multiplies by $3$: $g(x + 4) = 3(x + 4)^{2}$. The answer $3x^{2} + 4$ is $(f \circ g)(x)$, the other order.

blocks.text: In {{lesson:2.2}} you converted temperatures with $F = 1.8C + 32$. A composite can chain two conversions into one.

blocks.question: A thermometer reads in kelvin (K). The function $g(x) = x - 273.15$ converts $x$ K to degrees Celsius, and $f(x) = 1.8x + 32$ converts $x$ degrees Celsius to degrees Fahrenheit. (a) Find $(f \circ g)(x)$. (b) Find $(f \circ g)(300)$ and say what it means.
steps: Expand: $1.8x - 491.67 + 32 = 1.8x - 459.67$. This one function turns kelvin straight into degrees Fahrenheit.
So a temperature of $300$ K is $80.33\,^{\circ}\mathrm{F}$.
The order matters: $(g \circ f)(x)$ would treat $x$ as degrees Celsius, then subtract $273.15$ from a Fahrenheit value, which means nothing.

blocks.text: A composite only works where the output of $g$ is an input $f$ accepts. With $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ and $g(x) = x - 7$, $(f \circ g)(3) = f(-4)$, which doesn't exist. So $g(x)$ must lie in the [[domain|domain]] of $f$.

blocks.prompt: Let $f(x) = 4x - 1$ and $g(x) = x^{2} + 2$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Find $(g \circ f)(-1)$.
blocks.hint: Work out $f(-1)$ first, then put that number into $g$.

blocks.text: In a model, a composite chains quantities. If $g$ turns time into a number of items, and $f$ turns a number of items into a cost, then $f \circ g$ turns time straight into cost.
The output of $g$ must be the quantity $f$ expects as its input, in the same units. Swap the two and the composite usually changes, so say which step happens first.

blocks.question: A bureau changes euros into US dollars. $c(x) = 1.08x$ gives the dollars received for $x$ euros, and $k(x) = x - 12$ takes off a fee of $12$ units of whatever currency it is applied to. (a) Describe $(c \circ k)(x)$ and $(k \circ c)(x)$ in context. (b) Which is better for the customer, and by how much?
steps: (a) $(c \circ k)(x) = c(x - 12) = 1.08(x - 12)$: a fee of $12$ euros is taken first, then the rest is changed into dollars.
$(k \circ c)(x) = k(1.08x) = 1.08x - 12$: all $x$ euros are changed first, then a fee of $12$ dollars is taken.
So $k \circ c$ is better: the customer gets $0.96$ dollars more, whatever the amount. A fee of $12$ euros is worth $12.96$ dollars, more than a fee of $12$ dollars.

blocks.prompt: A weather balloon is $h(t)$ metres high $t$ minutes after launch. The air temperature, in degrees Celsius, at a height of $h$ metres is $T(h)$. What does $(T \circ h)(10)$ represent?
blocks.hint: $(T \circ h)(10) = T(h(10))$. What is $h(10)$, and what does $T$ do to it?

options.text: the air temperature at the balloon 10 minutes after launch
the height of the balloon when the air temperature is 10 degrees Celsius
the air temperature 10 metres above the ground
the time when the balloon is 10 metres high

blocks.explain: $h(10)$ is the balloon's height after $10$ minutes. $T$ turns that height into the air temperature there.

verify.truth: the air temperature at the balloon 10 minutes after launch

blocks.text: A composite model can give an equation you can't solve by hand. Write down the equation, then solve it with your GDC.

blocks.question: A car bought for $26\,000$ dollars is worth $V(t) = 26\,000(0.82)^{t}$ dollars after $t$ years. Its yearly insurance costs $I(V) = 350 + 0.045V$ dollars when the car is worth $V$ dollars. (a) Find $(I \circ V)(t)$. (b) Use your GDC to find when the insurance falls to $950$ dollars. Give your answer to 3 s.f.
steps: (b) Write down the equation: $350 + 1170(0.82)^{t} = 950$.
Graph $y = 350 + 1170(0.82)^{x}$ and $y = 950$, and find where they meet: $x = 3.3652\ldots$
Interpret: the insurance falls to $950$ dollars about $3.37$ years after the car is bought.
Another route: solve $I(V) = 950$ first, giving $V = 13\,333.3\ldots$, then solve $V(t) = 13\,333.3\ldots$ Keep the full value of $V$, not a rounded one.

blocks.prompt: A circular ripple has radius $r(t) = 0.6t + 0.2$ metres, $t$ seconds after a stone lands. Its area is $A(r) = \pi r^{2}$. Find the time when the area of the ripple is $10\text{ m}^{2}$, in seconds. Give your answer to 3 s.f.
blocks.hint: Form $(A \circ r)(t)$, set it equal to $10$, and keep only a positive time.
blocks.explain: Solve $\pi(0.6t + 0.2)^{2} = 10$. Then $0.6t + 0.2 = \sqrt{10/\pi} = 1.7841\ldots$, so $t = 2.6402\ldots \approx 2.64$ s. The negative root gives a negative time, so reject it.

blocks.text: Keeping a solution the context rules out, such as a negative time. Say which solution you reject, and why.
In {{lesson:2.2}} you met the [[inverse-function|inverse function]] $f^{-1}$. It undoes $f$: if $f(a) = b$, then $f^{-1}(b) = a$.
So doing $f$ and then $f^{-1}$ takes every input back to where it started. The same happens in the other order.

blocks.statement: For a function $f$ with an inverse, $(f \circ f^{-1})(x) = x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $f^{-1}$, and $(f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $f$.
blocks.why: $f^{-1}$ reverses whatever $f$ does, and $f$ reverses whatever $f^{-1}$ does.

blocks.text: Use this to check an inverse you have found: compose the two and you should get back $x$.
To find $f^{-1}(x)$, undo $f$ with algebra:
1. Write $y = f(x)$.
2. Swap $x$ and $y$. This step earns a method mark, so show it.
3. Rearrange to make $y$ the subject, and write the result as $f^{-1}(x) = \ldots$.
4. The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the [[range|range]] of $f$. Check one value: if $f(a) = b$, then $f^{-1}(b)$ should be $a$.
You may rearrange first and swap the letters last instead. Either order gives the same $f^{-1}(x)$.

blocks.question: A taxi fare is $F(d) = 3.5 + 2.5d$ dollars for a trip of $d$ km, where $d \ge 0$. (a) Find $F^{-1}(x)$. (b) Find $F^{-1}(21.5)$ and interpret it.
steps: (a) Write $y = 3.5 + 2.5x$, using $x$ for the input. Swap $x$ and $y$: $x = 3.5 + 2.5y$.
Make $y$ the subject: $2.5y = x - 3.5$, so $y = \frac{x - 3.5}{2.5} = 0.4x - 1.4$.
Interpret: a fare of $21.50$ dollars pays for a trip of $7.2$ km. $F^{-1}$ turns a fare back into a distance.

blocks.prompt: Let $f(x) = 4x - 9$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Which function $g$ gives $(f \circ g)(x) = x$?
blocks.hint: $g$ must undo $f$. $f$ multiplies by $4$ and then subtracts $9$. Undo those steps in reverse order.
blocks.explain: Add $9$, then divide by $4$: $g(x) = \frac{x + 9}{4}$. Check: $f\left(\frac{x + 9}{4}\right) = (x + 9) - 9 = x$. $\frac{1}{4x - 9}$ is $\frac{1}{f(x)}$, not the inverse.

blocks.text: Writing $f^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{f(x)}$. The $-1$ is a label meaning “inverse”, not a power. Find $f^{-1}$ by swapping $x$ and $y$ and rearranging.

blocks.question: An investment is worth $A(t) = 2000\mathrm{e}^{0.045t}$ dollars after $t$ years, where $t \ge 0$. (a) Find $A^{-1}(x)$. (b) State the domain of $A^{-1}$. (c) Find $A^{-1}(3000)$ to 3 s.f., and interpret it.
steps: Take natural logs: $0.045y = \ln\left(\frac{x}{2000}\right)$, so $A^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{0.045}\ln\left(\frac{x}{2000}\right)$.
(b) For $t \ge 0$, $A(t)$ starts at $A(0) = 2000$ and grows without limit. So the range of $A$ is $A(t) \ge 2000$, and the domain of $A^{-1}$ is $x \ge 2000$.
Interpret: the investment takes about $9.01$ years to grow to $3000$ dollars.

blocks.prompt: A car park charges $P(h) = 4 + 3.2h$ dollars for $h$ hours. Find $P^{-1}(20)$, the number of hours you can park for $20$ dollars.
blocks.hint: Solve $4 + 3.2h = 20$, or find $P^{-1}(x)$ first and substitute $20$.
blocks.explain: $P^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 4}{3.2}$, so $P^{-1}(20) = \frac{16}{3.2} = 5$. Twenty dollars buys $5$ hours of parking.

blocks.hint: Swap to get $x = 3 + \frac{8}{y - 1}$. Subtract $3$ first, then flip both sides.
blocks.explain: $x - 3 = \frac{8}{y - 1}$, so $y - 1 = \frac{8}{x - 3}$ and $f^{-1}(x) = 1 + \frac{8}{x - 3}$. The last option is $f$ itself.

blocks.text: “Interpret $f^{-1}(a)$”: write one sentence that links both quantities, with units, such as “a fare of $21.50$ dollars pays for a $7.2$ km trip”.
In {{lesson:2.2}} you saw that only a [[one-to-one-function|one-to-one function]] has an inverse. A parabola fails: a horizontal line can meet it twice.
Take $f(x) = (x - 1)^{2} + 2$. Both $x = -1$ and $x = 3$ give $6$, so $f^{-1}(6)$ would have two answers. On $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $f$ has no inverse.
Fix this by keeping only one side of the vertex. On $x \ge 1$ the graph only rises, so every output comes from one input.

blocks.alt: The parabola y equals f of x, with vertex (1, 2). A dashed horizontal line y equals 6 meets it twice, at x equals minus 1 and x equals 3. The left half, for x less than 1, is faint and dashed; the right half, for x at least 1, is solid. The curve y equals f inverse of x is the reflection of the solid half in the dashed line y equals x, starting at (2, 1).
blocks.caption: Keeping $x \ge 1$ makes $f(x) = (x - 1)^{2} + 2$ one-to-one. Its inverse is the reflection of that half in $y = x$.

blocks.statement: A function that only increases, or only decreases, over its domain is one-to-one, so it has an inverse. For a quadratic, restrict the domain to one side of the vertex: $x \ge h$ or $x \le h$, where $x = h$ is the axis of symmetry.
blocks.why: If the graph never turns back, no horizontal line can meet it twice.

blocks.text: Either side works, but each side gives a different inverse. With $x \le 1$, the same $f$ would have the inverse $1 - \sqrt{x - 2}$ instead of $1 + \sqrt{x - 2}$.
1. Find the vertex (complete the square, or use your GDC's minimum or maximum) and keep the side you are given.
2. Swap $x$ and $y$, and rearrange. A square root gives $\pm$: the restricted domain decides the sign. Say why.
3. The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of the restricted $f$, and the range of $f^{-1}$ is the restricted domain.

blocks.question: Let $f(x) = (x + 1)^{2} - 6$. (a) Show that $f$ has no inverse when its domain is $x \in \mathbb{R}$. (b) The domain is now restricted to $x \le -1$. Find $f^{-1}(x)$.
steps: (a) $f(-3) = (-2)^{2} - 6 = -2$ and $f(1) = 2^{2} - 6 = -2$. Two inputs share an output, so $f$ is not one-to-one and has no inverse.
(b) The vertex is $(-1, -6)$, and $x \le -1$ is its left side, so $f$ only decreases there. Swap: $x = (y + 1)^{2} - 6$.
Rearrange: $(y + 1)^{2} = x + 6$, so $y + 1 = \pm\sqrt{x + 6}$.
Choose the sign: the range of $f^{-1}$ is $y \le -1$, so $y + 1 \le 0$. Take the negative root: $f^{-1}(x) = -1 - \sqrt{x + 6}$.
Its domain is the range of the restricted $f$: $x \ge -6$. Check: $f(-3) = -2$, and $-1 - \sqrt{-2 + 6} = -3$.

blocks.text: Leaving $\pm$ in the inverse. An inverse is a function, so it gives one output: use the restricted domain to choose the sign, and say so.

blocks.prompt: Let $f(x) = 2x^{2} - 12x + 7$, for $x \ge k$. Find the smallest value of $k$ for which $f$ has an inverse.
blocks.explain: The axis is $x = \frac{12}{2 \times 2} = 3$. The parabola opens upwards, so it only increases for $x \ge 3$. Any smaller $k$ takes in both sides of the vertex.

blocks.hint: After swapping, you get $(y - 1)^{2} = 9 - x$. The range of $h^{-1}$ is $y \ge 1$: which root keeps $y - 1 \ge 0$?
blocks.explain: $y - 1 = \pm\sqrt{9 - x}$, and $y \ge 1$ needs the positive root, so $h^{-1}(x) = 1 + \sqrt{9 - x}$.

blocks.prompt: For the same function, $h(x) = 9 - (x - 1)^{2}$ with $x \ge 1$, state the domain of $h^{-1}$.
blocks.hint: The domain of $h^{-1}$ is the range of $h$. What is the largest value $h$ takes on $x \ge 1$?
blocks.explain: The largest value is $h(1) = 9$, and $h$ decreases from there, so the range of $h$ is $h(x) \le 9$. That is the domain of $h^{-1}$. $x \ge 1$ is the domain of $h$.

blocks.text: In a model, the context often restricts the domain for you. Time, length and speed can't be negative.

blocks.question: A car travelling at $v$ km/h needs $d(v) = 0.006v^{2} + 0.2v$ metres to stop, where $v \ge 0$. (a) Explain why $d$ has an inverse on this domain. (b) Use your GDC to find $d^{-1}(50)$. Give your answer to 3 s.f., and interpret it.
steps: (a) The vertex of $y = 0.006v^{2} + 0.2v$ is at $v = -\frac{0.2}{2 \times 0.006} \approx -16.7$, outside the domain. So for $v \ge 0$, $d$ only increases, and it is one-to-one.
(b) $d^{-1}(50)$ is the speed $v$ with $d(v) = 50$. Write down the equation: $0.006v^{2} + 0.2v = 50$.
Graph $y = 0.006x^{2} + 0.2x$ and $y = 50$ for $x \ge 0$, and find where they meet: $x = 76.129\ldots$
The equation also has a negative solution, $x = -109.46\ldots$, but it is outside the domain $v \ge 0$, so reject it.
Interpret: a car that needs $50$ m to stop was travelling at about $76.1$ km/h.

blocks.text: “Find $f^{-1}(x)$, stating its domain”: the domain earns its own mark. Give the range of $f$ as an inequality in $x$, and match the endpoint: $\le$ if $f$ reaches it, $<$ if it doesn't.
In $(f \circ g)(x)$, the function next to $x$ acts first: do $g$, then $f$. The output of $g$ must lie in the domain of $f$.
In context, $(f \circ g)(x)$ means “do the step $g$ models, then the step $f$ models”. Swapping the order usually changes the result.
To find $f^{-1}(x)$ for a one-to-one $f$: write $y = f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, then make $y$ the subject. The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$.
A function has an inverse only if it is one-to-one. A quadratic becomes one-to-one when its domain is restricted to one side of its vertex, $x \ge h$ or $x \le h$.
When rearranging gives $\pm\sqrt{\ }$, the restricted domain of $f$ (the range of $f^{-1}$) decides the sign.

mistakes: Composing in the wrong order. In $(f \circ g)(x)$ the function next to $x$ acts first, so substitute $g(x)$ into $f$.
Describing a composite in context without saying which step comes first. Say, for example, “the fee is taken before the money is converted”.
Leaving $\pm\sqrt{\ }$ in $f^{-1}(x)$. Use the restricted domain to reject one sign, and show why.
Giving the domain of $f^{-1}$ from its formula, or with the wrong endpoint. It is the range of $f$: use $\le$ where $f$ reaches the endpoint and $<$ where it doesn't.
Giving a negative time or speed as $f^{-1}(a)$ in a model. Check each solution against the domain and reject the ones outside it.
examTips: “Find $f^{-1}(x)$”: show the line where you swap $x$ and $y$. It earns a method mark even if the algebra slips later.
“Describe the meaning of $(f \circ g)(x)$” or “interpret”: answer in words about the context, saying which step happens first and naming the quantities with units.
To find $f^{-1}(a)$ without a formula, solve $f(x) = a$ on your GDC. Write down the equation first, then give the value in the domain, to 3 s.f.
